rewrite: This paper examines how green space coverage relates to surface temperature in Kota Mangrove Jaya, a tropical city where urban heat affects public health and energy use. We analyzed Landsat imagery from 2015 to 2025 across 74 administrative villages. Every 10 percent increase in vegetation cover corresponded to a 1.4 degree Celsius drop in average land surface temperature. Villages with less than 5 percent green space reached peak temperatures of up to 41.8 degrees Celsius in the dry season. Much of this pattern follows the replacement of rice fields with asphalt and metal roofing, which absorb heat and radiate it back. A household survey of 320 respondents found that residents of the hottest areas spent 27 percent more on electricity for cooling. The results support adding green infrastructure to urban planning.

NestNote puts your family's chores, meals, and schedules in one app.

Since launching in April 2025, it has been used by more than 60,000 families across Southeast Asia. The shared calendar syncs in real time for up to 8 family members.

The grocery list sorts items by aisle. Beta users cut their average shopping trip from 52 minutes to 31 minutes.

Parents can set screen-time rewards that unlock when kids finish assigned tasks.

All data is stored on servers in Singapore, and NestNote never sells personal information.

One reviewer from Penang said the app ended the era of the family whiteboard.

Premium costs USD 3.99 per month. New users get a 30-day free trial. Download NestNote.

The Makassar-Parepare line will run six new daily trips from 1 November, the Sulawesi Rail Authority announced on Thursday, 17 September 2026. Daily capacity will rise from 4,200 to 7,800 passengers.

Authority director Hasanuddin Baso said ridership surged after Barru Timur station opened in March. Weekend trains had been running at 112 percent of seated capacity, leaving many passengers standing for more than two hours.

Four additional train sets will be leased from a domestic manufacturer for Rp 64 billion. "Every new train set must meet the accessibility standard for wheelchair users," Baso told a press conference.

Local business groups welcomed the expansion and said it could bring more tourists to the western coast. Some commuters worry that fares may go up next year.

AquaSense Labs, a small startup from Kendari, won the top prize at the 2026 Indonesia Green Innovation Awards for a low-cost sensor that detects heavy metal contamination in drinking water within 15 minutes.

The award, presented in Jakarta on 8 September, includes a grant of Rp 750 million to scale up production.

Founder Nadia Kusumawati said the idea came from a 2024 survey that found unsafe lead levels in 31 of 90 village wells near nickel processing sites. Laboratory testing costs around Rp 1.2 million per sample and takes up to three weeks, she said, so most villages never test.

Each AquaSense unit costs Rp 450,000 and can be reused for about 200 tests. The judging panel called it "practical enough for a village health volunteer to operate alone."

The company plans to distribute 1,000 units across Southeast Sulawesi by mid-2027.

A landslide cut the only road between Kampung Lembah Hijau and the district capital at around 3:40 a.m. on Monday, isolating around 1,350 residents.

It followed two days of torrential rain that dropped 186 millimeters on the area. The local disaster agency said mud and fallen trees buried a 70-meter stretch of road. Officials said illegal logging upstream had stripped the vegetation that normally holds the slope in place.

Volunteers are carrying emergency food in on foot. "heavy equipment must reach the site within 48 hours to prevent food shortages," said the agency's head, Yulius Kambuaya.

Two excavators were dispatched on Tuesday morning, 22 September 2026, but continued rain has slowed the work. No casualties have been reported. Authorities have pledged to investigate the logging in the watershed.

The evidence on remote work is less tidy than either its enthusiasts or its skeptics suggest. A 2026 survey by the Meridian Workforce Institute found that 58 percent of Indonesian office workers prefer a hybrid schedule of two or three office days. Only 12 percent wanted to work fully from home, largely because cramped housing makes a quiet workspace hard to find.

In my view, that points to something policy debates often overlook: remote work is only as good as the home it happens in.

The Jakarta-based firm Kirana Analytics offers a monthly allowance of Rp 500,000 for co-working spaces. Its policy states that "no employee should have to work from a bedroom unless they choose to." Flexibility without support is a transfer of costs.

Exams have long been treated as a fair, objective measure of student achievement. It is worth asking what they measure and what they leave out.

In Sulawesi Raya, the 2025 national exam results showed that 67 percent of students in urban schools passed mathematics, against 34 percent in rural schools. I would argue that gap says more about access to trained teachers than about student ability. According to the Provincial Education Office, rural districts there have one certified mathematics teacher for every 210 students.

Some schools have tried portfolio assessment. Sekolah Alam Tepian Danau reported a 22 percent rise in attendance after dropping weekly drill tests. Its principal put it simply: "we grade the project, not the panic."

Tests will not disappear overnight, nor should they.
